description.narrative: The Project is expected to supply 319 GWh/year of low-cost renewable electricity in Bulgaria, equivalent to a 1.1% increase. It will also contribute to reducing CO2 emissions by 240,000 tons of CO2 equivalent per year by 2025 in a country where 40% of its generation stems from fossil fuels. At the market level, the Project is expected to enhance competitiveness by demonstrating the feasibility of large-scale merchant RE financing in a context where electricity generation remains state-dominated and private investments have faced uncertainty due to policy shifts. A successful implementation may generate replication, leading to more private investment in this space. It will also improve resilience by diversifying the energy mix away from fossil fuels while helping to reach Bulgarias RE targets.

The proposed investment will support the development of the St George Solar Project (the Project), a 199 MW solar photovoltaic (PV) plant to be located near the town of Silistra in Northeastern Bulgaria. The project will be developed by R-Engineering EOOD (the Company), an SPV established by Rezolv Energy (https://rezolv.energy/). Rezolv is an independent renewable energy producer focused on investments in renewables in the Eastern European energy market. It is wholly owned by Actis LLC. The project consists of the construction, operation, and maintenance of the solar plant. Construction work is expected to commence in mid-2024 and will take approximately 12 months. The plant is anticipated to be in operation for 35 years. The Project is expected to sell generated electricity through the Independent Bulgarian Power Exchange IBEX and under commercial PPAs.]
